svg.title: Equipotentials of an electric ray
svg.desc: Two computed panels treating the electric ray as a dipole, positive head on the right and negative tail on the left. (a) In open water: nearly circular equipotentials surround each end; the zero-potential equipotential is the straight perpendicular bisector between head and tail; positive loops lie on the head side and negative loops on the tail side, and no equipotential encloses both ends. Larger loops have smaller potentials and are pinched toward the middle, never becoming circles around the ray. (b) Above a grounded conducting hull along the bottom: the hull is itself the zero equipotential, and the equipotentials between the ray and the hull are flattened and squeezed to run along it, while those above the ray look much as in (a). The potential increases toward the head and away from the tail.
